items.title: The same verb, a different direction

states.label: Toward the speaker
states.note: The other person is leaving, and the speaker wants to be waited for.

states.label: Away from the speaker
states.en: Wait here until I come back.
states.note: The speaker is leaving and asks the other person to stay until the speaker returns.

items.caption: The last word turns the waiting toward or away from the speaker. The English translations include the situation in which each phrase is used.

items.title: Directions measured from the event

points.label: aʻe
points.note: Up stays up whoever is speaking.

points.label: ifo
points.note: Down stays down whoever is speaking.

points.label: ʻese
points.note: This direction is measured from a point fixed by the event, rather than from the speaker.

items.caption: These three words take their bearings from the event or thing itself. This is a schematic map of their directions, not a compass.

items.title: Hear the direction

data.question: Which direction does the marked word give?

prompts.sm: Na alu vave atu le tama.
prompts.why: The describing word *vave* comes before the direction word *atu*, which points away from the speaker.

prompts.sm: Sā nofo aʻe ai le tama.
prompts.why: The direction word *aʻe* comes after the verb and before *ai*.

prompts.sm: ʻO le pusi i lalo ifo o le fale.
prompts.why: The direction word *ifo* follows the spatial noun and keeps its downward direction.

items.intro: Read the whole sentence, then choose the direction supplied by its direction word.
